newsitem.title: USA: NYS Gov "hopeful" on federal transportation aid.
newsitem.headline: NYS Gov "hopeful" on federal transportation aid.

text.p: New York State Gov George Pataki on Wednesday said that he was encouraged by the Clinton Administration's recent proposal on the huge, federal transportation bill now up for renewal.

"Just last week, I was with the (U.S.) Secretary of Transportation in New York, and they are looking at an administrative proposal that he says we will not be unhappy with," Pataki told reporters in Albany.

The governor, who added that he had no details, noted that New York State faces a stiff fight because New York City relies so heavily on mass transit, and formulas used to divide the federal aid that are based on how much individual states pay in gasoline taxes can work against the state.

States are intensely competing to ensure that they get their fair share under the Intermodal Surface Transportation and Efficiency Act, which gives them an average of $22 billion a year and which Congress is expected to renew before it expires on September 30. New York State is fighting to keep its approximately $1.8 billion piece of the pie.
